findings.title: OAuth integration is the documented model for customer-connected apps
findings.detail: OAuth integrations let each user authorize the app and use an access token tied to that user. Tokens must be used as OAuth bearer tokens, not personal or internal tokens.

evidence.quote: Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to
a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

findings.title: Multi-workspace customers require a public integration
findings.detail: A connection limited to selected workspaces cannot serve other customer organizations and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Use a public integration for customers outside your workspace. Installation scope cannot be changed later.

evidence.quote: ​ Installation scope Choose Or select 1 or more workspaces when creating your integration. Only those workspaces can install it, and it cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make
your app available to any workspace, create a public integration .
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation. If you later need to make the app available to any workspace, create a new integration.

findings.title: Request the Read content capability for both read actions
findings.detail: Read content gives access to read existing content. Retrieving a page and its property values requires this capability plus access to each page.

evidence.quote: Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
Your connection needs read content capabilities and access to the page. For relations, formulas, and rollups, share the related databases too.

findings.title: Do not request Insert or Update content capabilities
findings.detail: Insert content and Update content are separate capabilities that allow creating and changing content. Leave both unselected to honor the no-write requirement.

steps.detail: In the Developer portal, create a new connection as a public integration. Add redirect URIs and select only Read content. Leave Insert and Update content unselected. Done when the connection exists and its Configuration tab shows OAuth client ID and secret.
steps.doneWhen: Connection saved with Read content only and redirect URI set.

steps.title: Implement the authorization and token-exchange callback
steps.detail: Build the authorization redirect and callback. Exchange the returned code at the token endpoint using Basic auth with client ID and secret, grant_type authorization_code, and the same redirect URI. Keep secrets server-side. Done when the callback code path exists and is ready to run.
steps.doneWhen: Callback and token exchange code exists without secrets in client code.

evidence.quote: Open the Configuration tab to find your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret . Use them to implement the OAuth authorization flow .
Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .
Content-Type : application/json { "grant_type" : "authorization_code" , "code" : "e202e8c9-0990-40af-855f-ff8f872b1ec6" , "redirect_uri" : "https://example.com/auth/notion/callback" }

steps.title: Authorize one representative test workspace (test account)
steps.detail: Using a test workspace you control, open the connection's authorization URL from the Configuration tab. Review the capability prompt, select one test page on the page picker, and approve. Your callback should receive a code and exchange it for an access token. Expected: access token returned. Boundary check: confirm the prompt lists only Read content.
steps.doneWhen: An access token is issued for the test workspace with one selected test page.

evidence.quote: 1 The user visits the connection’s authorization URL. Find this URL in the Configuration tab of your connection in the Developer portal.
2 Notion presents a prompt describing the connection’s capabilities — what it will be able to do in the user’s workspace.
3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.
4 After the user approves, Notion redirects them to your redirect URI with a temporary authorization code.
5 Your connection exchanges the code for an access token, which is used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user.

steps.detail: Call the documented block children route for the test page with the same OAuth token and Notion-Version header. Replace the example block ID with your test page ID.
